title: Operator resilience escape hatches and simulation roadmap
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This document defines the catalog of operator "escape hatches" (operator-initiated safe modes and manual interventions) used to preserve SLOs and protect customer traffic when automation or primary fallbacks fail. It also defines a repeatable simulation lab and a 12-month roadmap to validate, automate, and instrument those escape hatches across the platform. The intention is to reduce mean time to safe state (MTTS) and operator cognitive load during high-severity incidents.

Background and motivation:
- Redwood platform provides automated fallbacks (model variants, regional routing, burst capacity). In rare multi-failure scenarios we rely on human-operated "escape hatches" to keep customer-facing services available.
- Recent postmortems identified inconsistent operator procedures, missing telemetry, and untested escape hatch paths as root causes for prolonged partial outages.
- This playbook codifies escape hatch types, preconditions, dashboards, test recipes, and ownership to make operator actions deterministic and safe.

Who should read this:
- Platform operators and oncall engineers
- Platform SRE and eng-platform feature owners
- Incident commanders and escalation managers
- Developer advocates who will implement telemetry hooks

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: LLM inference serving surface (runtime, allocator, KV cache layer, routing, cache prefetch), platform control plane actions (route drain, model swap), and operator-facing tools (CLI, operator UI).
- Non-goal: Replacing fully automated fallback policies — this document complements automation and is intended for degraded/edge cases only.

Escape hatch catalog (short reference):
1) Global read-only mode (Control plane)
   - Purpose: Stop write operations to stateful control-plane resources (e.g., tenant config writes, quota mutations) while allowing inference read path to continue.
   - Precondition: Control-plane write latency > 5s for 3 consecutive minutes or API error rate > 1% that correlates to config writes.
   - Effect: Block POST/PUT/DELETE to /v1/tenants, /v1/quotas for 10m; set header X-Redwood-Escape: readonly.
   - Owner: control-plane-team; operator CLI: rw-escape readonly enable

2) Regional model-swap to compatible quantized variant (Serving runtime)
   - Purpose: Rapidly replace served model with a lighter quantized compatible variant when memory pressure or kernel OOMs are detected.
   - Precondition: Node OOMs > 2% or GPU memory pressure > 92% across pool for 2 minutes despite autoscale.
   - Effect: Per-region traffic shifted to model: "gptx-8q-compat-v2" with automatic KV cache flush for affected shards.
   - Owner: serving-runtime; operator UI action: "Swap model (region)" or CLI: rts model swap --region eu-west-1 --from gptx-16b --to gptx-8q-compat-v2 --force

3) Tenant soft-quarantine (Traffic control)
   - Purpose: Isolate a noisy tenant affecting multi-tenant tail-latency SLOs but preserve best-effort capacity.
   - Precondition: Tenant token-cost spike > 3x baseline for 10m and cross-tenant tail-latency 99.9th > 1.5x SLO.
   - Effect: Apply QoS profile: rate-limit 80% of new requests, preserve in-flight tokens. Notify tenant owner.
   - Owner: platform-allocator team; CLI: allocator quarantine --tenant tenant-1234 --limit 0.2

4) Global prefix-cache disable and fallback to stateless batching (Caching)
   - Purpose: Temporarily disable prefix/KV caching when cache corruption or cross-shard inconsistency is suspected.
   - Precondition: Cache inconsistency alarms + SIGCOUNTER > 50 across 3 shards or incorrect generation hashes observed in golden prompt checks.
   - Effect: Set runtime flag: runtime.cache.mode=stateless, enable aggressive batching window 50ms.
   - Owner: runtime-core; operator CLI: runtime set-flag cache.mode stateless --reason "cache-corruption"

5) Progressive degraded-mode notice (Customer-facing)
   - Purpose: Trigger internal and external communications and enable automatic product-level degradations (e.g., limited tokens, lower token-quality model).
   - Precondition: SLO burn rate > 200% for 15 minutes across production clusters.
   - Effect: Notify growth/CS, add banner in Console, enable cost-based routing fallback.
   - Owner: product-ops & growth; operator action: comms-trigger --severity high

Escape hatch safety checklist (pre-authorization before action):
- Confirm incident severity and scope with incident lead.
- Verify that automated fallbacks have been attempted and logs show failures.
- Check SLOs and customer impact: 95th, 99th, error-rate, and token-billing anomalies.
- Confirm owner team and oncall contact are present to monitor for 30 minutes post-action.
- Have rollback steps available and tested in the lab (see simulation recipes).

Dashboards and alerts to support escape hatches:
- Mandatory dashboards (operator quick-filter presets):
  - "Escape Hatch Cockpit" (single-pane): aggregated SLO burn, node memory heatmap, model-variant distribution, cache-inconsistency counters, tenant-blame top-10.
  - "Regional Model Pressure" per-region view with GPU memory buckets (0-64%, 65-80%, 81-92%, >92%) and OOM event timeline.
  - "Tenant Burst Monitor": rolling 1h token-rate anomaly score, top offending tenants, and recent mutation RPC failures.

- Alert thresholds (suggested, tune per-region):
  - gpu.memory_pressure > 0.92 for 2m -> severity P2 (paging)
  - prefix_cache.hash_mismatch > 5/min across cluster -> severity P1 (investigate/block)
  - cross_tenant_tail_latency_99.9 > 1.5x SLO for 10m -> severity P1
  - tenant_token_rate_spike (zscore>4 over 10m) -> severity P2

- Alert actions mapping table (operator guide):
  - P1 cache/hash_mismatch -> consider "Global prefix-cache disable" hatch; gather recent golden-prompt diffs first.
  - P1 tail-latency -> evaluate tenant-quarantine in parallel with regional model-swap.
  - P2 memory_pressure -> model-swap; if swap fails, enable regional preemption/burst-eviction.

Safe rollout and rollback procedures (step-by-step):
- Example: Regional model-swap (eu-west-1)
  1. Confirm telemetry: gpu.memory_pressure > 0.92 and OOMs present in the last 3 commits.
  2. Run dry-run query: rts model check-compat --from gptx-16b --to gptx-8q-compat-v2 --region eu-west-1 and review compatibility report.
  3. Notify oncall and post to incident channel with ETA and expected impact.
  4. Execute swap for 10% of traffic: rts model swap --region eu-west-1 --from gptx-16b --to gptx-8q-compat-v2 --percentage 10 --wait 60s
  5. Observe: tail latency, error rates, and KV cache hits for 10 minutes. If stable, increase to 50% then 100% using increments of 20% every 5 minutes.
  6. Rollback command: rts model swap --region eu-west-1 --from gptx-8q-compat-v2 --to gptx-16b --force or revert using traffic-slice restore.

Simulation lab: recipes and acceptance criteria
- Purpose: Validate escape hatches under controlled fault injection and ensure runbooks produce the expected safe state without human error.
- Lab environment: operator-lab-redwood (isolated Kubernetes clusters, synthetic tenants, mirrored telemetry pipeline).
- Minimum test matrix (run quarterly):
  * Cache corruption injection: flip hash on shard-3 and verify that "Global prefix-cache disable" produces stable response quality and keeps 95th latency within 1.3x baseline.
  * Model OOM storm: artificially increase model memory footprint to produce 30% node OOMs; validate regional model-swap completes and tail latencies reduce below SLO within 8 minutes.
  * Tenant noise event: synthetic tenant issues 5x normal token-rate; validate tenant-quarantine throttle and no cross-tenant SLO regression.

- Test steps (example: cache corruption):
  1. Create synthetic workload: lab-cli workload create --prompts-file golden-prompts.json --tenant lab-escape-01 --qps 150
  2. Inject fault: lab-cli inject cache-hash-flip --shard shard-3 --duration 600s
  3. Operator follows playbook: runtime set-flag cache.mode stateless --reason "lab-cache-test"
  4. Monitor metrics for 15 minutes. Acceptance: 95th latency < 1.3x baseline and generation-consistency checkpoint shows no unexplained deltas.

Instrumentation and observability requirements:
- Every escape hatch action must generate a structured audit event with fields: operator_id, hatch_id, preconditions_snapshot, rollback_command, expected_degradation, and incident_ref. (See audit event schema in /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/audit-event-schema-2025.json)
- Recommended metrics to emit at action start/complete: hatch.latency.start, hatch.latency.completed, hatch.effectiveness.score (0-1), hatch.rollback.invoked (0/1).
- Dashboards must include a historical heatmap of hatch usage by operator and by service to detect overuse.

Automation roadmap (12 months):
- Q1: Implement structured audit events (hatch.*) and add "Escape Hatch Cockpit" dashboard template.
- Q2: Automate precondition checks and dry-run compatibility verification for model-swap and affinity changes.
- Q3: Expose safe, idempotent CLI wrappers for tenant-quarantine and cache-mode toggles with built-in rollback timers.
- Q4: Integrate simulation lab runs into CI (run nightly synthetic smoke tests, weekly deep-simulations in staging).

Operational metrics and SLIs related to escape hatches:
- MTTS (Mean time to safe-state) target: <= 7 minutes for model-swap hatches, <= 5 minutes for tenant-quarantine.
- Hatch rollback rate target: < 10% within 60 minutes of action.
- Hatch cognitive load metric: number of operator steps (goal < 6 for any hatch).

Roles and responsibilities:
- Incident lead: decides whether hatch is required and signs off.
- Owning team (per hatch): executes and monitors hatch, owns rollback.
- Platform telemetry: ensures dashboards, alert mappings, and audit logs exist.
- Product-ops & growth: owns customer comms flow for progressive degraded-mode notices.

Training and runbook maintenance:
- Quarterly tabletop drills for all oncall engineers covering at least two escape hatch types.
- Runbook owners must update playbook after any simulation where acceptance criteria fail, within 2 weeks of the test.

Retrospective template (for each hatch use):
1. Incident summary (what happened, timeline)
2. Which hatch was applied and why
3. Time-to-safe-state and impact metrics
4. What worked / what failed
5. Action items (owner + due date)
6. Add to lab test matrix? (yes/no)

Appendices:
- Appendix A: Example audit event (JSON)
  {
    "operator_id": "maya.patel",
    "hatch_id": "regional-model-swap-eu-west-1-v2",
    "preconditions_snapshot": "gpu.memory_pressure=0.93;oom=12",
    "rollback_command": "rts model swap --region eu-west-1 --from gptx-8q-compat-v2 --to gptx-16b --force",
    "expected_degradation": "latency 10-20% increase 95th",
    "incident_ref": "INC-2026-1093"
  }

- Appendix B: CLI quick cheatsheet
  - Check model compatibility: rts model check-compat --from <src> --to <dst> --region <r>
  - Partial swap: rts model swap --region <r> --from <src> --to <dst> --percentage 10 --wait 60s
  - Quarantine tenant: allocator quarantine --tenant <id> --limit 0.2 --reason "noisy-reqs"
  - Toggle cache modes: runtime set-flag cache.mode <stateless|normal> --reason <text>

Notes and open questions:
- How frequently should the hatch historical heatmap be surfaced to leadership? (proposal: weekly summary, monthly deep-dive)
- Should a "hatch usage quota" exist per operator to reduce risky interventions? (proposal: soft quota + escalation review after 3 uses per week)
